## About this session

This session is a free-standing introduction to [duckdb in R](https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/clients/r). In this session, we'll use the `duckdb` package as a database back-end, and demonstrate how to interact with that back-end using the DBI package. You might also be interested in [our session on dbplyr](r_training/dbplyr_dtplyr.html) as an alternative means of using your duckdb database.


::: {.callout-tip collapse="false" appearance="default" icon="true"}
## Session resources
+ you don't need any infrastructure apart from an R setup
+ see the setup chunk below for packages
+ you should have a reasonable working knowledge of R
:::

## Setup

Create a new project, and install and attach packages:

```{r}
# install.packages("pak")
# pak::pak("duckdb")
# pak::pak("DBI")
# pak::pak("palmerpenguins")

library(duckdb)
library(dplyr) # surprisingly useful for working with databases
library(DBI)
library(palmerpenguins)

```

## What?

Duckdb is a lightweight database backend that allows you to create comparatively high-performance databases on your local computer easily. Here's the minimal example:

```{r}
mem_con <- dbConnect(duckdb()) 
```

This connection object represents an in-memory duckdb database. To add some data to that database, we can use `duckdb::dbWriteTable`:

```{r}
duckdb::dbWriteTable(conn = mem_con, name = "pengs", value = penguins)

# dplyr::copy_to(dest = mem_con,df = penguins, name = "pengs") # just beware the names (and order) of arguments differs from the otherwise-similar dplyr::copy_to function
```

There are then a range of options for retrieving data. `DBI::dbGetQuery` executes a SQL query on your database, and returns a standard R data.frame:

```{r}
DBI::dbGetQuery(mem_con, "SELECT * FROM pengs WHERE species = 'Adelie' AND year = 2007")
```
You can also do much the same thing in a more R-friendly way with [a bit of d(b)plyr](r_training/dbplyr_dtplyr.html):

```{r}
tbl(mem_con, "pengs") |>
  filter(species == "Adelie" & year == 2007) |>
  collect()
```

## On-disk databases

```{r}
disk_con <- dbConnect(duckdb(), dbdir = "data/disk_con.duckdb") # the dbdir argument in the connection object is the only change
```

```{r}
#| eval: false
duckdb::dbWriteTable(conn = disk_con, name = "pengs", value = penguins)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
duckdb::dbWriteTable(conn = disk_con, name = "pengs", value = penguins, overwrite = T)
```

```{r}
DBI::dbGetQuery(disk_con, "SELECT * FROM pengs WHERE species = 'Adelie' AND year = 2007")
```


## Referencing tibbles/data.frames

Like creating a virtual table. Doesn't copy any data, good for practice and preview.

```{r}
duckdb_register(mem_con, "ref_pengs", penguins)

DBI::dbGetQuery(mem_con, "SELECT * FROM ref_pengs WHERE species = 'Adelie' AND year = 2007")
```

## Big chunky data

Scotland makes available national prescribing data [aggregated by dispenser and by medication type](https://www.opendata.nhs.scot/dataset/prescriptions-in-the-community/resource/15e675c7-ac8d-4000-a690-b70a2d3d3a76). That full data-set is pretty chunky indeed - roughly a couple of million rows of data per month, which is probably a bit larger than we can comfortably deal with in a training session, so we'll use a slice of this data showing prescriptions in NHS Grampian to explore DuckDB as a tool for working with big(ish) data.

Here's some data-wranging code, which probably isn't going to be of interest:

```{r}
#| code-fold: true

# dispensers_2026july <- phsopendata::get_resource("15e675c7-ac8d-4000-a690-b70a2d3d3a76") |>
#   filter(HBT == "S08000020") # grab your Grampian

# dispensers_2026july |>
# readr::write_rds(here::here("r_training/data/dispensers_2026july.rds"))

```

You should [download the sample data](data/dispensers_2026july.rds) - approximately 200MB - and save it somewhere sensible in your current R project. We can then read that data as a tibble, which we can then register into our on-disk DB

```{r}
data_path <- "r_training/data/dispensers_2026july.rds" # change that to suit

dispensers_2026july <- readr::read_rds(here::here(data_path))

# disk_con <- dbConnect(duckdb(), dbdir = "data/disk_con.duckdb") # if you didn't set-up an on-disk DB above

duckdb_register(disk_con, "dispensers_2026july", dispensers_2026july, overwrite = T) # otherwise overwriting a table causes duckdb_register to fail
```


## Simple filter and summarise

We could do that in dplyr:

```{r}
dispensers_2026july |>
  filter(stringr::str_detect(BNFItemCode, "0209000A0AAA")) |>
  summarise(.by = c(BNFItemCode, BNFItemDescription), PaidQuantity = sum(PaidQuantity))
```

Here's the SQL version:

```{r}
DBI::dbGetQuery(disk_con, "SELECT BNFItemCode, BNFItemDescription, SUM(PaidQuantity) AS PaidQuantity,  FROM dispensers_2026july WHERE BNFItemCode LIKE '0209000A0AAA%' GROUP BY BNFItemCode, BNFItemDescription")
```

Or a transitional form using dbplyr:

```{r}
tbl(disk_con, "dispensers_2026july") |>
  filter(stringr::str_detect(BNFItemCode, "0209000A0AAA")) |>
  summarise(.by = c(BNFItemCode, BNFItemDescription), PaidQuantity = sum(PaidQuantity)) |>
  collect()
```

## Benchmarking

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| eval: false
library(microbenchmark)

presc_bench <- microbenchmark::microbenchmark(

  dplyr = dispensers_2026july |>
    filter(stringr::str_detect(BNFItemCode, "0209000A0AAA")) |>
    summarise(.by = c(BNFItemCode, BNFItemDescription), PaidQuantity = sum(PaidQuantity)),
  
  sql = DBI::dbGetQuery(disk_con, "SELECT BNFItemCode, BNFItemDescription, SUM(PaidQuantity) AS PaidQuantity,  FROM dispensers_2026july WHERE BNFItemCode LIKE '0209000A0AAA%' GROUP BY BNFItemCode, BNFItemDescription"),

  dbplyr = tbl(disk_con, "dispensers_2026july") |>
    filter(stringr::str_detect(BNFItemCode, "0209000A0AAA")) |>
    summarise(.by = c(BNFItemCode, BNFItemDescription), PaidQuantity = sum(PaidQuantity)) |>
    collect()
)

presc_bench |>
  readr::write_rds(here::here("r_training/data/presc_bench.rds")) |>
  autoplot()
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

library(microbenchmark)
readr::read_rds(here::here("r_training/data/presc_bench.rds")) |>
  ggplot2::autoplot()
```
